# Vexev Raises $6M to Accelerate U.S. Commercialization of Autonomous Vascular Imaging Platform

Vexev logo

SYDNEY, Australia, August 6, 2026 \- Australian medical robotics company [Vexev](https://www.vexev.com/) today announced it has raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and U.S. commercialization of VxWave, its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform, designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging. The raise brings Vexev’s total funding to date to $19 million.

Cardiovascular disease is the world's leading cause of death, claiming nearly 20 million lives each year.¹ Yet access to high-quality vascular imaging remains constrained by specialist availability and inconsistent image acquisition.

...

html) , the VxWave demonstrated a 94% scanning success rate for autonomous vascular imaging by non-specialist clinical staff, with the potential ability to standardize vascular imaging designed to improve consistency and potentially decreasing time to diagnosis and treatment.

"We believe high-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available," said John Carroll, PhD, co-founder and CEO of Vexev. "We are starting with dialysis patients because the clinical need is clear, but our vision is much broader: to build an autonomous imaging platform that helps clinicians make faster, more consistent and more informed decisions across vascular disease."

Beyond dialysis vascular access, Vexev intends to expand its autonomous imaging platform into additional vascular disease applications like cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease, while building the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions.
The fundraise round included participation from existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate and Horizon, together with new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures and Alumni Ventures. Funding will support regulatory activities, manufacturing scale-up and commercialization.

"Having worked closely with Vexev for several years, I have seen the development of its impressive robot- and AI-based techniques for vascular imaging," said Anupam Agarwal, MD, Senior Vice President for Medicine and Dean of the Marnix E. Heersink School of Medicine at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, and past president of the American Society of Nephrology. "The company's initial focus on dialysis vascular access addresses an important challenge for patients and providers, and I believe this technology has the potential to bring meaningful innovation to dialysis patients with vascular access challenges."

# Vexev raises $6M to support robotic ultrasound tech

August 6, 2026 By [Sean Whooley](https://www.massdevice.com/author/sean-whooley/)

Vexev U.S. Renal Care VxWave robotic ultrasound (1) The Vexev and U.S. Renal Care teams with the VxWave robotic system. [Image courtesy of Vexev/U.S. Renal Care] [Vexev](https://www.massdevice.com/tag/vexev/) announced today that it raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the progress of its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform.

Existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate and Horizon participated in the round.
New investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures and Alumni Ventures all joined as well. The company plans to use funds to support regulatory activities, manufacturing scale-up and commercialization.

This round brings Vexev’s total funding to $19 million to date.

Sydney, Australia-based Vexev develops VxWave, an ultrasound platform designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging. Funding comes on the heels of [successful results in a multi-site clinical study shared last fall](https://www.massdevice.com/vexev-robotic-ultrasound-study-meets-endpoints/) .

VxWave combines robotics, AI and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition. The company is developing the platform for upper limb vascular imaging, targeting dialysis vascular access as an initial application. It integrates advanced robotics, machine learning and ultrasound signal processing.
This combination creates a 3D vascular model and detailed report to deliver insights into vascular access points at the point of care.

Beyond the current target area, the company expects to bring its platform to additional vascular disease applications. It also hopes to build the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions.

“We believe high-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available,” said John Carroll, co-founder and CEO of Vexev. “We are starting with dialysis patients because the clinical need is clear, but our vision is much broader: to build an autonomous imaging platform that helps clinicians make faster, more consistent and more informed decisions across vascular disease.”

### About Vexev

Vexev logo

Vexev

Surry Hills, New South Wales , Australia Healthcare 33 employees Founded 2018 14\.5M USD total raised [Website](https://www.vexev.com/)

Vexev is a medical technology startup, founded in 2018. It has raised $14.5M across 2 funding rounds, most recently a $6M Venture round in August 2026, from investors including NeoTribe Ventures, Startmate and Blackbird Ventures.
### About This Round

Vexev has raised $6 million to push its autonomous vascular imaging platform into the United States, taking the Sydney medical-robotics company to $19 million raised in total. Existing backers Blackbird Ventures , NeoTribe Ventures , Startmate and Horizon all returned, joined by new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13 , Bioshore Ventures and Alumni Ventures . No lead was disclosed. [1](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vexev-raises-6m-to-accelerate-us-commercialization-of-autonomous-vascular-imaging-platform-302842976.html) [2](https://www.massdevice.com/vexev-raises-6m-robotic-ultrasound/)

Vexev's product, VxWave, is a robotic ultrasound system that acquires vascular images without a sonographer driving the probe. Its first market is dialysis vascular access, where a patient's arteriovenous fistula has to be checked repeatedly to catch stenosis before the access fails. In a multi-site clinical study run with U.S.
Renal Care, non-specialist staff achieved a 94% scanning success rate on the autonomous system. Co-founder and chief executive John Carroll frames the goal as decoupling imaging from staffing: "High-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available." [1](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vexev-raises-6m-to-accelerate-us-commercialization-of-autonomous-vascular-imaging-platform-302842976.html)

The money goes to regulatory work, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation. That ordering matters, because VxWave is still investigational — it does not yet hold FDA 510(k) clearance — so the round is buying the path to market rather than the market itself. Beyond dialysis access, the company points at cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease as the follow-on indications. [1](https://www.prnewswire.
com/news-releases/vexev-raises-6m-to-accelerate-us-commercialization-of-autonomous-vascular-imaging-platform-302842976.html) [2](https://www.massdevice.com/vexev-raises-6m-robotic-ultrasound/)

The interesting thing about this raise is its size. Six million dollars is a small cheque for a medical device company standing in front of an FDA submission, a manufacturing ramp and a US commercial launch simultaneously — the three most expensive things a device company does, and Vexev has named all three as uses of funds. Read charitably, that is a company with a clearance pathway short enough and a contract manufacturer close enough that it does not need more; the 510(k) route for an ultrasound acquisition system with a well-characterised predicate is genuinely cheaper than a de novo. Read less charitably, it is a bridge with a press release. The tell will be the dialysis chains: U.S.
Renal Care already ran the study, and a device whose entire value proposition is that a technician rather than a sonographer can use it only pays for itself inside a network large enough to have a sonographer shortage. If a second chain signs before clearance, the small round was correctly sized. If not, the next one will not be optional.

[Read the announcement](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vexev-raises-6m-to-accelerate-us-commercialization-of-autonomous-vascular-imaging-platform-302842976.html)
